Accessibility

Building accessible components with Karibase

Overview

Karibase is committed to making web accessibility achievable for all. Our components follow WCAG 2.1 AA standards and include proper ARIA attributes, keyboard navigation, and screen reader support.

Accessibility is built into the framework from the ground up, ensuring that your applications are usable by everyone, regardless of their abilities or disabilities.

WCAG Compliance

Karibase components meet WCAG 2.1 AA requirements:

  • Perceivable: Information and UI components must be presentable to users in ways they can perceive
  • Operable: UI components and navigation must be operable
  • Understandable: Information and the operation of the UI must be understandable
  • Robust: Content must be robust enough to be interpreted reliably by a wide variety of user agents

Keyboard Navigation

All interactive components are keyboard accessible:

html
<!-- Keyboard accessible button -->
<button class="kb-btn kb-btn-primary" tabindex="0">
  Click me
</button>

<!-- Keyboard accessible link -->
<a href="#" class="kb-link" tabindex="0">
  Navigate here
</a>

ARIA Attributes

Components include appropriate ARIA attributes:

html
<!-- Modal with ARIA attributes -->
<div class="kb-modal-overlay" 
     role="dialog" 
     aria-modal="true" 
     aria-labelledby="modal-title">
  <h2 id="modal-title">Modal Title</h2>
  <button aria-label="Close modal">×</button>
</div>

<!-- Progress bar with ARIA -->
<div class="kb-progress" role="progressbar" 
     aria-valuenow="75" 
     aria-valuemin="0" 
     aria-valuemax="100">
  <div class="kb-progress-bar" style="width: 75%"></div>
</div>

Screen Readers

Optimized for screen reader compatibility:

  • Semantic HTML elements
  • Proper heading hierarchy
  • Descriptive link text
  • Form labels and descriptions
  • Error messages with proper associations

Color Contrast

All color combinations meet WCAG AA contrast ratios:

  • Normal text: 4.5:1 contrast ratio
  • Large text: 3:1 contrast ratio
  • UI components: 3:1 contrast ratio
  • Focus indicators: 3:1 contrast ratio

Focus Indicators

Clear focus states for keyboard navigation:

html
/* Focus styles */
.kb-btn:focus-visible {
  outline: 3px solid var(--kb-primary);
  outline-offset: 2px;
}

.kb-input:focus {
  border-color: var(--kb-primary);
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(234, 40, 69, 0.2);
}

Best Practices

Follow these accessibility best practices:

  • Use semantic HTML elements
  • Provide alternative text for images
  • Ensure form inputs have associated labels
  • Test with keyboard navigation
  • Validate with screen readers
  • Use color as an enhancement, not the only indicator
  • Provide sufficient time for users to read and interact
  • Avoid content that flashes more than 3 times per second
  • Make sure all functionality is available from a keyboard

Testing Accessibility

Test your application with these tools:

  • WAVE: Web Accessibility Evaluation Tool
  • axe DevTools: Browser extension for accessibility testing
  • Lighthouse: Built-in Chrome accessibility audit
  • NVDA / JAWS: Screen reader testing
  • Keyboard-only navigation: Test without mouse
